turns.code:
import monitor

def test_is_stuck():
    # Test case 1: No stuck jobs (all completed or running within grace period)
    events = [
        "job=a running at=10",
        "job=a completed at=20",
        "job=b running at=5"
    ]
    now = 30
    grace = 10
    result = monitor.is_stuck(events, now, grace)
    assert result == [], f"Expected empty list, got {result}"

    # Test case 2: One stuck job (running and older than grace)
    events = [
        "job=a running at=5",
        "job=a running at=10",  # Update to a newer running event
        "job=b completed at=20"
    ]
    now = 25
    grace = 10
    result = monitor.is_stuck(events, now, grace)
    assert result == [], f"Expected empty list, got {result}"

    # Test case 3: Stuck job (running and older than grace)
    events = [
        "job=a running at=5",
        "job=b completed at=20"
    ]
    now = 25
    grace = 10
    result = monitor.is_stuck(events, now, grace)
    assert result == ['a'], f"Expected ['a'], got {result}"

    # Test case 4: Multiple stuck jobs
    events = [
        "job=a running at=5",
        "job=b running at=10",
        "job=c completed at=20"
    ]
    now = 30
    grace = 15
    result = monitor.is_stuck(events, now, grace)
    assert result == ['a', 'b'], f"Expected ['a', 'b'], got {result}"

    # Test case 5: Edge case (equal to grace is not stuck)
    events = [
        "job=a running at=15"
    ]
    now = 30
    grace = 15
    result = monitor.is_stuck(events, now, grace)
    assert result == [], f"Expected empty list, got {result}"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_is_stuck()
